# US Hot Springs by the Numbers — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Publish a citable annual data report at `soaktrail.com/reports/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers`, generated by a build-time pipeline that also backfills derived fields (elevation, remoteness, soakability/safety) into the 6 regional D1 databases.

**Architecture:** Python pipeline script (`scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py`) fetches all springs from the 6 regional D1 DBs via `wrangler d1 execute`, derives elevation (USGS EPQS, cached) and remoteness (haversine vs `data/uscities.csv`), classifies soakability with rule-based safety logic, then writes `sites/soaktrail/src/data/by_the_numbers.json` + a public CSV + per-DB backfill SQL. A prerendered Astro page renders the JSON. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers-design.md`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12 (`uv run`, stdlib only for the script), pytest via `uv run --with pytest` for tests (NOT added to project deps), Astro 5 prerendered page + Tailwind, Cloudflare D1 via wrangler CLI.

## Global Constraints

- Repo root is the working directory for the script (wrangler auth/config resolves from root).
- Scripts run as `uv run scripts/<name>.py`; stdlib only (csv, json, math, sqlite-free, subprocess, time, urllib.request).
- Tests run as `uv run --with pytest pytest scripts/test_by_the_numbers.py -v` — do NOT add pytest to `pyproject.toml`.
- Region slug → child site URL mapping (must match `sites/soaktrail/src/lib/regions.ts` exactly):
  `washington → https://www.washingtonhotsprings.com`, `alaska → https://www.alaskahotsprings.com`, `shasta → https://www.shastahotsprings.com`, `colorado → https://www.soakcolorado.com`, `rockies → https://www.soaktherockies.com`, `desert → https://www.desertsoak.com`
- D1 database names (from root `wrangler` config): `desertsoak-db` (desert), `soaktherockies-springs-db` (rockies), `soakcolorado-springs-db` (colorado), `shastahotsprings-db` (shasta), `washingtonhotsprings-db` (washington), `alaskahotsprings-db` (alaska).
- Spring deep-link convention: `{child_site}/springs/{slug}`.
- Dataset license shown on the page: CC-BY 4.0 (attribution → backlinks; chosen for a citation asset — flag to user at review).
- The generated JSON and CSV MUST be committed — CI builds (`deploy-sites.yml`) build from the repo checkout, not from local data.
- Soaktrail deploy: `cd sites/soaktrail && npm run build && npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=saoktrail --branch=main` (never `wrangler deploy`).

## File Structure

- Create `migrations/007_report_enrichment.sql` — ALTER TABLE adding `soakable`, `safety_notes`.
- Modify `migrations/001_unified_springs_schema.sql` — fold the 2 new columns into the CREATE TABLE (repo convention, see its header comment about 003).

- Create `scripts/test_by_the_numbers.py` — pytest tests for pure functions.
- Create `sites/soaktrail/src/components/RankingTable.astro` — shared ranking table (rows + metric type).
- Create `sites/soaktrail/src/pages/reports/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.astro` — the report page.
- Generated (committed): `sites/soaktrail/src/data/by_the_numbers.json`, `sites/soaktrail/public/data/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.csv`.
- Generated (NOT committed): `migrations/out/007_backfill_<db>.sql` × 6, `data/elevation_cache.json`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the skeleton + fetch**

Create `scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the 'US Hot Springs by the Numbers' annual report dataset.

Fetches all springs from the 6 regional D1 databases, derives elevation
(USGS EPQS) and remoteness (nearest place >= 1,000 pop in data/uscities.csv),
classifies soakability/safety, then writes:
  - sites/soaktrail/src/data/by_the_numbers.json   (report page data)
  - sites/soaktrail/public/data/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.csv
  - migrations/out/007_backfill_<db>.sql           (D1 backfill, applied manually)

Usage:
    uv run scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py            # full run
    uv run scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py --no-fetch # reuse cached fetch (dev)
"""

import csv
import json
import math
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CITIES_CSV = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "uscities.csv"
ELEV_CACHE = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "elevation_cache.json"
FETCH_CACHE = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "report_springs_fetch.json"
REPORT_JSON = REPO_ROOT / "sites" / "soaktrail" / "src" / "data" / "by_the_numbers.json"
REPORT_CSV = REPO_ROOT / "sites" / "soaktrail" / "public" / "data" / "us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.csv"
BACKFILL_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "migrations" / "out"

# db name -> region slug (must match root wrangler d1_databases config)
D1_DATABASES = {
    "desertsoak-db": "desert",
    "soaktherockies-springs-db": "rockies",
    "soakcolorado-springs-db": "colorado",
    "shastahotsprings-db": "shasta",
    "washingtonhotsprings-db": "washington",
    "alaskahotsprings-db": "alaska",
}

# region slug -> child site URL (must match sites/soaktrail/src/lib/regions.ts)
REGION_SITES = {
    "washington": "https://www.washingtonhotsprings.com",
    "alaska": "https://www.alaskahotsprings.com",
    "shasta": "https://www.shastahotsprings.com",
    "colorado": "https://www.soakcolorado.com",
    "rockies": "https://www.soaktherockies.com",
    "desert": "https://www.desertsoak.com",
}

COLUMNS = (
    "slug, name, lat, lon, state, region, temperature_f, elevation_ft, "
    "distance_to_town_mi, nearby_town, development, access_type, fees, "
    "fee_amount_usd, description"
)


def parse_d1_output(raw: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Parse `wrangler d1 execute --json` output into a row list."""
    data = json.loads(raw)
    if not data or not data[0].get("success"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"D1 query failed: {raw[:300]}")
    return data[0]["results"]


def fetch_db(db_name: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Fetch all springs from one regional D1 database via wrangler."""
    cmd = [
        "npx", "wrangler", "d1", "execute", db_name, "--remote", "--json",
        "--command", f"SELECT {COLUMNS} FROM springs",
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"wrangler failed for {db_name}: {proc.stderr[:500]}")
    rows = parse_d1_output(proc.stdout)
    if not rows:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{db_name} returned 0 springs — refusing to build an incomplete report")
    for row in rows:
        row["_db"] = db_name
    return rows


def fetch_all_springs(no_fetch: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Fetch every spring from all 6 DBs (or reuse the cached fetch with --no-fetch)."""
    if no_fetch:
        return json.loads(FETCH_CACHE.read_text())
    springs: list[dict] = []
    for db_name in D1_DATABASES:
        rows = fetch_db(db_name)
        print(f"  {db_name}: {len(rows)} springs")
        springs.extend(rows)
    FETCH_CACHE.write_text(json.dumps(springs))
    return springs


def main() -> None:
    no_fetch = "--no-fetch" in sys.argv
    springs = fetch_all_springs(no_fetch)
    print(f"Total springs: {len(springs)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```python
NOT_SOAKABLE_PHRASES = ("not soakable", "not a soaking", "not recommended for soaking")


def classify_safety(spring: dict) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Rule-based soakability classification (see spec: safety rules table).

    First match wins. Temp thresholds: sustained soaking unsafe >~110°F;
    >=120°F scalds within minutes. Resorts/developed sites with hot sources
    manage pool temps, so they stay soakable with a note.
    """
    desc = (spring.get("description") or "").lower()
    access = (spring.get("access_type") or "").lower()
    temp = spring.get("temperature_f")
    dev = (spring.get("development") or "").lower()

    if access == "not soakable" or any(p in desc for p in NOT_SOAKABLE_PHRASES):
        return "not_soakable", (
            "Listed as a geothermal feature, not a soaking site. Do not enter the water."
        )
    if temp is None:
        return "unknown", None
    if temp >= 120:
        if dev == "primitive":
            return "too_hot", (
                f"Source temperature {temp}°F can scald in minutes. Water may cool "
                "downstream — verify pool temperature before entering."
            )
        return "soakable", (
            f"Source water emerges at {temp}°F; soaking pools are cooled/managed. "
            "Follow posted guidance on site."
        )
    if temp >= 110 and dev == "primitive":
        return "caution", (
            f"Source temperature {temp}°F is at or above safe soaking limits. "
            "Test carefully before entering."
        )
    return "soakable", None
```

Add to `scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py` (above `main`):

```python
EPQS_URL = "https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json?x={lon}&y={lat}&units=Feet&wkid=4326&includeDate=False"
MIN_CITY_POP = 1_000


def haversine_mi(lat1: float, lon1: float, lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:
    """Great-circle distance in miles."""
    r = 3958.7613
    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)
    dp = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
    dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
    a = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * r * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))


def load_cities(path=CITIES_CSV) -> list[tuple[float, float, str, str]]:
    """Load US places with population >= MIN_CITY_POP from the SimpleMaps CSV."""
    cities = []
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            try:
                pop = int(row.get("population") or 0)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if pop < MIN_CITY_POP:
                continue
            try:
                cities.append((float(row["lat"]), float(row["lng"]), row["city"], row["state_id"]))
            except (KeyError, ValueError):
                continue
    return cities


def _elev_cache_key(lat: float, lon: float) -> str:
    return f"{lat:.4f},{lon:.4f}"


def derive_elevation(springs: list[dict]) -> int:
    """Fill elevation_ft from USGS EPQS, cached in data/elevation_cache.json.

    Returns the number of springs whose elevation could not be determined.
    """
    cache = json.loads(ELEV_CACHE.read_text()) if ELEV_CACHE.exists() else {}
    failures = 0
    fetched = 0
    for s in springs:
        lat, lon = s.get("lat"), s.get("lon")
        if lat is None or lon is None:
            s["elevation_ft"] = None
            failures += 1
            continue
        key = _elev_cache_key(lat, lon)
        if key not in cache:
            url = EPQS_URL.format(lat=lat, lon=lon)
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=20) as resp:
                    value = json.load(resp).get("value")
                cache[key] = round(float(value)) if value not in (None, "", -1000000) else None
                fetched += 1
                time.sleep(0.15)  # be polite to the USGS endpoint
            except Exception as exc:  # network/parse failure: record as unknown, keep going
                print(f"  elevation lookup failed for {s.get('slug')}: {exc}")
                cache[key] = None
            if fetched % 50 == 0 and fetched:
                ELEV_CACHE.write_text(json.dumps(cache))  # checkpoint long runs
        s["elevation_ft"] = cache[key]
        if cache[key] is None:
            failures += 1
    ELEV_CACHE.write_text(json.dumps(cache))
    return failures


def derive_remoteness(springs: list[dict], cities: list[tuple[float, float, str, str]]) -> None:
    """Set distance_to_town_mi / nearby_town to the nearest >=MIN_CITY_POP place."""
    for s in springs:
        lat, lon = s.get("lat"), s.get("lon")
        if lat is None or lon is None or not cities:
            continue
        best = min(cities, key=lambda c: haversine_mi(lat, lon, c[0], c[1]))
        s["distance_to_town_mi"] = round(haversine_mi(lat, lon, best[0], best[1]), 1)
        s["nearby_town"] = f"{best[2]}, {best[3]}"
```

```python
    print("  soakable classes:", dict(Counter(s["soakable"] for s in springs)))
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Add to `scripts/build_by_the_numbers.py` (above `main`):

```python
RANK_LIMIT = 20
ROW_KEYS = (
    "slug", "name", "state", "region", "temperature_f", "elevation_ft",
    "distance_to_town_mi", "nearby_town", "development", "access_type",
    "soakable", "safety_notes",
)


def _row(s: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: s.get(k) for k in ROW_KEYS}


def build_report(springs: list[dict], edition: int) -> dict:
    """Compute rankings + aggregate stats for the report."""
    temped = [s for s in springs if s.get("temperature_f") is not None]
    soakable_temped = [s for s in temped if s["soakable"] in ("soakable", "caution")]
    elevated = [s for s in springs if s.get("elevation_ft") is not None]
    remote = [s for s in springs if s.get("distance_to_town_mi") is not None]
    access_rank = {"hike": 0, "boat": 0, "4wd": 1, "dirt": 2, "drive-up": 3, "paved": 4, "resort": 5}

    development_split: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for dev in ("resort", "developed", "primitive"):
        group = [s for s in springs if (s.get("development") or "").lower() == dev]
        fees = [s["fee_amount_usd"] for s in group if s.get("fee_amount_usd") is not None]
        temps = [s["temperature_f"] for s in group if s.get("temperature_f") is not None]
        development_split[dev] = {
            "count": len(group),
            "with_fees": sum(1 for s in group if s.get("fees") and str(s["fees"]).lower() not in ("", "none", "free")),
            "avg_fee_usd": round(sum(fees) / len(fees), 2) if fees else None,
            "avg_temp_f": round(sum(temps) / len(temps), 1) if temps else None,
        }

    region_development = []
    for region in REGION_SITES:
        group = [s for s in springs if s.get("region") == region]
        region_development.append({
            "region": region,
            "total": len(group),
            "resort": sum(1 for s in group if s.get("development") == "resort"),
            "developed": sum(1 for s in group if s.get("development") == "developed"),
            "primitive": sum(1 for s in group if s.get("development") == "primitive"),
        })

    by_state = []
    states = sorted({s.get("state") for s in springs if s.get("state")})
    for st in states:
        group = [s for s in springs if s.get("state") == st]
        hottest = max((s for s in group if s.get("temperature_f") is not None),
                      key=lambda s: s["temperature_f"], default=None)
        by_state.append({
            "state": st,
            "count": len(group),
            "hottest": {"slug": hottest["slug"], "name": hottest["name"],
                        "temperature_f": hottest["temperature_f"]} if hottest else None,
        })
    by_state.sort(key=lambda x: -x["count"])

    return {
        "edition": edition,
        "generated_at": date.today().isoformat(),
        "stats": {
            "total": len(springs),
            "regions": len({s.get("region") for s in springs if s.get("region")}),
            "states": len(states),
            "with_temperature": len(temped),
            "temp_min_f": min((s["temperature_f"] for s in temped), default=None),
            "temp_max_f": max((s["temperature_f"] for s in temped), default=None),
            "elevation_pending": sum(1 for s in springs if s.get("elevation_ft") is None),
            "safety": {
                cls: sum(1 for s in springs if s["soakable"] == cls)
                for cls in ("soakable", "caution", "too_hot", "not_soakable", "unknown")
            },
        },
        "rankings": {
            "hottest_soakable": [_row(s) for s in sorted(
                soakable_temped, key=lambda s: -s["temperature_f"])[:RANK_LIMIT]],
            "hottest_recorded": [_row(s) for s in sorted(
                temped, key=lambda s: -s["temperature_f"])[:RANK_LIMIT]],
            "highest": [_row(s) for s in sorted(
                elevated, key=lambda s: -s["elevation_ft"])[:RANK_LIMIT]],
            "most_remote": [_row(s) for s in sorted(
                remote, key=lambda s: (-s["distance_to_town_mi"],
                                       access_rank.get(s.get("access_type") or "", 9)))[:RANK_LIMIT]],
        },
        "development_split": development_split,
        "region_development": region_development,
        "by_state": by_state,
    }


def write_report_json(report: dict) -> None:
    REPORT_JSON.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    REPORT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    print(f"  wrote {REPORT_JSON.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}")


def write_csv(springs: list[dict]) -> None:
    REPORT_CSV.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fields = [
        "slug", "name", "state", "region", "lat", "lon", "temperature_f",
        "elevation_ft", "distance_to_town_mi", "nearby_town", "development",
        "access_type", "fees", "fee_amount_usd", "soakable", "safety_notes", "site_url",
    ]
    with open(REPORT_CSV, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        for s in sorted(springs, key=lambda s: (s.get("state") or "", s.get("name") or "")):
            row = {k: s.get(k) for k in fields}
            row["site_url"] = f"{REGION_SITES[s['region']]}/springs/{s['slug']}" if s.get("region") in REGION_SITES else None
            writer.writerow(row)
    print(f"  wrote {REPORT_CSV.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}")


def _sql_str(value) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return "NULL"
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return str(value)
    return "'" + str(value).replace("'", "''") + "'"


def emit_backfill(springs: list[dict]) -> list[Path]:
    """Emit one UPDATE-per-spring SQL file per regional DB."""
    BACKFILL_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths = []
    for db_name in D1_DATABASES:
        lines = []
        for s in springs:
            if s.get("_db") != db_name:
                continue
            lines.append(
                "UPDATE springs SET "
                f"elevation_ft = {_sql_str(s.get('elevation_ft'))}, "
                f"distance_to_town_mi = {_sql_str(s.get('distance_to_town_mi'))}, "
                f"nearby_town = {_sql_str(s.get('nearby_town'))}, "
                f"soakable = {_sql_str(s.get('soakable'))}, "
                f"safety_notes = {_sql_str(s.get('safety_notes'))} "
                f"WHERE slug = {_sql_str(s['slug'])};"
            )
        path = BACKFILL_DIR / f"007_backfill_{db_name}.sql"
        path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        paths.append(path)
        print(f"  wrote {path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} ({len(lines)} updates)")
    return paths
```

And replace the end of `main()` (after the soakability classification loop) with:

```python
    edition = date.today().year
    report = build_report(springs, edition)
    print("Writing outputs...")
    write_report_json(report)
    write_csv(springs)
    emit_backfill(springs)
    print("Done. Review migrations/out/007_backfill_*.sql, then apply per DB:")
    for db_name in D1_DATABASES:
        print(f"  npx wrangler d1 execute {db_name} --remote --file migrations/out/007_backfill_{db_name}.sql")
```

`sites/soaktrail/src/components/RankingTable.astro`:

```astro
---
import { stateName, accessLabel } from '../lib/states';
import { REGIONS } from '../lib/regions';

interface Row {
  slug: string;
  name: string;
  state: string;
  region: string;
  temperature_f: number | null;
  elevation_ft: number | null;
  distance_to_town_mi: number | null;
  nearby_town: string | null;
  development: string | null;
  access_type: string | null;
  soakable: string;
  safety_notes: string | null;
}

interface Props {
  rows: Row[];
  metric: 'temp' | 'elev' | 'remote';
}

const { rows, metric } = Astro.props;
const siteFor = (region: string) => REGIONS.find((r) => r.slug === region)?.childSite;
const needsCaution = (row: Row) => row.soakable === 'too_hot' || row.soakable === 'not_soakable';
---

<ol class="divide-y divide-sa-dark/10 rounded-lg border border-sa-dark/10 bg-white/60">
  {rows.map((row, i) => (
    <li class="px-4 py-3">
      <div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
        <div class="flex items-center gap-3 min-w-0">
          <span class="font-mono text-sm text-sa-dark/40 w-6 text-right shrink-0">{i + 1}</span>
          <div class="min-w-0">
            <p class="font-display font-bold text-sa-dark truncate">
              {needsCaution(row) && <span class="text-sa-copper" title={row.safety_notes ?? 'Not safe to soak'}>&#9888;&#65038; </span>}
              {siteFor(row.region) ? (
                <a href={`${siteFor(row.region)}/springs/${row.slug}`} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="hover:text-sa-copper">{row.name}</a>
              ) : row.name}
            </p>
            <p class="text-xs text-sa-dark/50 capitalize mt-0.5">
              {stateName(row.state)}
              {row.nearby_town ? ` · near ${row.nearby_town}` : ''}
              {accessLabel(row.access_type) ? ` · ${accessLabel(row.access_type)}` : ''}
              {row.development ? ` · ${row.development}` : ''}
            </p>
            {needsCaution(row) && row.safety_notes && (
              <p class="text-xs text-sa-copper mt-1 normal-case">{row.safety_notes}</p>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="text-right shrink-0">
          {metric === 'temp' && <p class="font-mono font-bold text-sa-copper">{row.temperature_f}°F</p>}
          {metric === 'elev' && <p class="font-mono font-bold text-sa-copper">{row.elevation_ft?.toLocaleString()} <span class="text-xs font-normal text-sa-dark/50">ft</span></p>}
          {metric === 'remote' && <p class="font-mono font-bold text-sa-copper">{row.distance_to_town_mi} <span class="text-xs font-normal text-sa-dark/50">mi</span></p>}
        </div>
      </div>
    </li>
  ))}
</ol>
```

```astro
---
import BaseLayout from '../../layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
import Breadcrumbs from '../../components/Breadcrumbs.astro';
import RankingTable from '../../components/RankingTable.astro';
import { stateName } from '../../lib/states';
import { REGIONS } from '../../lib/regions';
import report from '../../data/by_the_numbers.json';

export const prerender = true;

const regionName = (slug: string) => REGIONS.find((r) => r.slug === slug)?.name ?? slug;
const canonical = 'https://soaktrail.com/reports/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers';
const csvUrl = 'https://soaktrail.com/data/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.csv';
const title = `US Hot Springs by the Numbers: ${report.edition} Annual Report`;
const description = `Data-driven rankings of America's hot springs: hottest, highest, and most remote, plus resort vs. primitive breakdowns — from SoakTrail's dataset of ${report.stats.total} documented springs.`;

const datasetSchema = {
  '@context': 'https://schema.org',
  '@type': 'Dataset',
  name: title,
  description,
  url: canonical,
  creator: { '@type': 'Organization', name: 'SoakTrail', url: 'https://soaktrail.com' },
  temporalCoverage: String(report.edition),
  spatialCoverage: { '@type': 'Place', name: 'United States' },
  distribution: { '@type': 'DataDownload', encodingFormat: 'text/csv', contentUrl: csvUrl },
  isAccessibleForFree: true,
  license: 'https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/',
  dateModified: report.generated_at,
};

const breadcrumbSchema = {
  '@context': 'https://schema.org',
  '@type': 'BreadcrumbList',
  itemListElement: [
    { '@type': 'ListItem', position: 1, name: 'Home', item: 'https://soaktrail.com/' },
    { '@type': 'ListItem', position: 2, name: 'Reports', item: canonical },
    { '@type': 'ListItem', position: 3, name: title, item: canonical },
  ],
};

    <section id="most-remote" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">Most remote springs</h2>
      <p class="text-sa-dark/80 mb-4">
        Ranked by straight-line distance to the nearest town of 1,000+ people; hike/boat access
        breaks ties. These demand real backcountry preparation.
      </p>
      <RankingTable rows={report.rankings.most_remote} metric="remote" />
    </section>

    <section id="resort-vs-primitive" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">Resort vs. primitive</h2>
      <div class="overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-sa-dark/10 bg-white/60">
        <table class="w-full text-sm">
          <thead>
            <tr class="border-b border-sa-dark/10 text-left text-sa-dark/60">
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium">Class</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Springs</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Share</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Charge fees</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Avg fee</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Avg source temp</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody class="divide-y divide-sa-dark/10">
            {(['resort', 'developed', 'primitive'] as const).map((dev) => {
              const d = report.development_split[dev];
              return (
                <tr>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 font-display font-bold text-sa-dark capitalize">{dev}</td>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{d.count}</td>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{Math.round(100 * d.count / report.stats.total)}%</td>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{d.with_fees}</td>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{d.avg_fee_usd != null ? `$${d.avg_fee_usd}` : '—'}</td>
                  <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{d.avg_temp_f != null ? `${d.avg_temp_f}°F` : '—'}</td>
                </tr>
              );
            })}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <div class="overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-sa-dark/10 bg-white/60 mt-4">
        <table class="w-full text-sm">
          <thead>
            <tr class="border-b border-sa-dark/10 text-left text-sa-dark/60">
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium">Region</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Total</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Resort</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Developed</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Primitive</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody class="divide-y divide-sa-dark/10">
            {report.region_development.map((r) => (
              <tr>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-display font-bold text-sa-dark">{regionName(r.region)}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{r.total}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{r.resort}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{r.developed}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{r.primitive}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="by-state" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">By state</h2>
      <div class="overflow-x-auto rounded-lg border border-sa-dark/10 bg-white/60">
        <table class="w-full text-sm">
          <thead>
            <tr class="border-b border-sa-dark/10 text-left text-sa-dark/60">
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium">State</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium text-right">Springs</th>
              <th class="px-4 py-3 font-medium">Hottest spring</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody class="divide-y divide-sa-dark/10">
            {report.by_state.map((s) => (
              <tr>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-display font-bold text-sa-dark">{stateName(s.state)}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-right font-mono">{s.count}</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3">{s.hottest ? `${s.hottest.name} (${s.hottest.temperature_f}°F)` : '—'}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="safety" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20 rounded-lg border border-sa-copper/30 bg-sa-copper/5 p-6">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">Soaking safety</h2>
      <ul class="list-disc list-inside text-sa-dark/80 space-y-2">
        <li><strong>Source temperature is not pool temperature.</strong> Figures here are measured at the source. Springs often cool as water flows into soaking pools — or they don't.</li>
        <li><strong>Water above ~110°F is unsafe for sustained soaking; at 120°F it scalds in minutes.</strong> {report.stats.safety.too_hot} springs in this dataset have primitive (unmanaged) sources at or above 120°F.</li>
        <li><strong>Not every thermal feature is a soaking site.</strong> {report.stats.safety.not_soakable} entries in the dataset are geothermal features you should not enter at all.</li>
        <li>Always test the water with a hand or thermometer before entering, and follow posted guidance at developed sites.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section id="methodology" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">Methodology</h2>
      <div class="text-sa-dark/80 space-y-3">
        <p>
          Dataset: {report.stats.total} hot springs from SoakTrail's six regional databases
          (Washington, Alaska, Shasta, Colorado + New Mexico, Northern Rockies, Desert Southwest),
          pulled {report.generated_at}. Temperatures are source temperatures from site research
          and public records.
        </p>
        <p>
          Elevations come from the USGS 3DEP Elevation Point Query Service at each spring's
          coordinates. Remoteness is the straight-line (haversine) distance to the nearest
          incorporated place with population ≥ 1,000 (SimpleMaps US Cities dataset) — it
          understates true travel effort for hike-in springs.
        </p>
        <p>
          Soakability is classified by rule: features described as not soakable are excluded from
          soaking rankings; primitive sources ≥ 120°F are flagged too hot to enter; primitive
          sources 110–119°F carry a caution; developed/resort sites with hot sources are listed as
          soakable because their pools are managed. {report.stats.elevation_pending > 0 &&
            `${report.stats.elevation_pending} springs are missing elevation data.`}
        </p>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="cite" class="mt-12 scroll-mt-20">
      <h2 class="font-display text-2xl font-bold text-sa-dark mb-3">Cite this report</h2>
      <div class="rounded-lg border border-sa-dark/10 bg-white/60 p-5 space-y-4">
        <div>
          <h3 class="font-display text-base font-bold text-sa-dark">APA</h3>
          <p class="text-sm text-sa-dark/80 mt-1 font-mono">
            SoakTrail. ({report.edition}). <em>US hot springs by the numbers: {report.edition} annual report</em> [Data set]. SoakTrail. {canonical}
          </p>
        </div>
        <div>
          <h3 class="font-display text-base font-bold text-sa-dark">Plain text</h3>
          <p class="text-sm text-sa-dark/80 mt-1 font-mono">
            SoakTrail, "US Hot Springs by the Numbers: {report.edition} Annual Report," {canonical} (accessed [your access date]).
          </p>
        </div>
        <p class="text-sm text-sa-dark/70">
          The underlying data is available as a <a href="/data/us-hot-springs-by-the-numbers.csv" class="text-sa-copper hover:underline">CSV download</a> and
          licensed <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-sa-copper hover:underline">CC-BY 4.0</a> —
          use it freely with attribution. Updated annually at this URL.
        </p>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>
</BaseLayout>
```

## Self-Review Notes

- Spec coverage: URL/citation/JSON-LD/CSV → Task 6; rankings (hottest/highest/most-remote/resort-vs-primitive/safety) → Tasks 3+5; D1 write-back → Tasks 1+5+7; annual refresh → spec documents the procedure, script is re-runnable (EPQS cache).
- Type consistency: `_row()` emits exactly `ROW_KEYS`; RankingTable's `Row` interface matches those keys; `build_report` consumers in the page use `report.rankings.*`, `report.development_split`, `report.region_development`, `report.by_state`, `report.stats.*` — all defined in Task 5.
- The page reads `report.edition`/`generated_at` from JSON (no hardcoded year).
